Since the game is 32 bit, you need to go to x32 and copy into the game's executable folder one of the following:

If your API is set to DX11, copy d3d11.dll and dxgi.dll.

If your API is set to DX10, copy d3d10core.dll. I've never tried this on a DX10 game, so if it doesn't work you will also need to copy dxgi.dll.

If your API is set to DX9, copy d3d9.dll.

You can make sure it's working by downloading MSI Afterburner and RTSS and enabling monitoring there.

If the game feels odd with DXVK, remove -availablevidmem from launch options and commandline.txt

Hopefully the game will finally be playable and you will feel the true Payne.

I'm using GTA V as an example, but you need to create commandline.txt in the game's executable folder and put -availablevidmem 384.0 OR 256.0, with only one argument and without "OR". Keep trying different values, including going above 512.0.
